page: Microsoft Azure L24aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptographic acceleration with AES and SHA_NI. Memory capacity totals 192 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation.

A defining characteristic of the L24aos_v4 is its bundled local high-speed storage array, providing 17,279 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and does not feature discrete GPU hardware accelerators. System memory throughput reaches 73.69 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB block reads and 56.07 GB/sec on writes, supporting data-dense input and output pipelines.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-quartile compute capability with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,083 and a multi-core score of 15,915. Stress-ng single-core processing also scores within the top 25 percent, while multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics sit within the median 50 percent tier. For machine learning tasks, quantized small-model LLM generation reaches 338.79 tokens per second, placing it in the top 10 percent, although 70-billion-parameter prompt processing drops into the bottom quartile due to host memory limits and lack of specialized matrix engines like AMX.

Cost efficiency for this instance is closely linked to its dense local NVMe storage and high memory-to-core ratio, which eliminates the need to attach multiple external managed disks for high-IOPS applications. The primary tradeoff lies in the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage, requiring application-level replication. The hardware configuration is ideally structured for large distributed databases, NoSQL engines, transactional data stores, search indexing, and real-time analytical workloads requiring high local throughput.

It provides 192 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 17,279 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU supports advanced vector instruction sets, including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, achieving top-quartile Geekbench single-core (2,083) and multi-core (15,915) results. Without discrete GPUs, larger language model workloads remain restricted, yet small-model text generation places in the top tier. Qualitative cost efficiency is realized through integrated NVMe storage density, eliminating dependencies on standalone high-IOPS disk volumes. L24aos_v4 is engineered for IOPS-intensive transactional databases, NoSQL clusters, search indexing, and big data processing pipelines.
